chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Uthman ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

'What is your view — if I were to narrate a hadith to you this year, then you came to me next year and I narrated something contrary to it, which of the two would you take?' He said: I said, 'I would take the later one.' So he said to me: 'May God have mercy on you.'

key_terms.بِالْأَخِيرِ: The latter/more recent — the later narration takes precedence
key_terms.بِخِلَافِهِ: Contrary to it — a narration that contradicts the earlier one
key_terms.رَحِمَكَ اللَّهُ: May God have mercy on you — a supplication indicating approval of the answer
key_terms.مِنْ قَابِلٍ: In the coming year / next year — classical expression for the following year

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about following the most recent hadith when there is a contradiction between narrations?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) poses a hypothetical question to a companion: if the Imam gives two contradictory narrations at different times, which should be followed? The companion answers he would follow the more recent one, and the Imam approves with a supplication of mercy. This hadith establishes the principle of tarjih (preference) by recency — the later narration abrogates or supersedes the earlier one in cases of apparent contradiction, a fundamental principle in Shia hadith methodology.
